assumptions: UNTESTED: at least one coordinate family has a stable eight-term expansion advantage rather than lying inside random-set variance.
HEURISTIC: 31 replicates per constructor provide a useful exploratory toy-scale percentile screen, not a family-wise significance test or asymptotic distribution.
MODEL-BOUND: exact uniform-order support-map work models an online fixed-curve lookup and not optimized hardware bandwidth.
HEURISTIC: binary-pow and 64-byte lookup charges are disclosed cost proxies rather than measured hardware costs.
falsification_conditions: No coordinate family reaches the preregistered support and frontier percentiles against both null families in six of nine clean instances spanning all sizes and seeds.
A sampled support-order aggregate differs from the exact uniform-order expectation or another preregistered aggregate by more than 25 percent.
A candidate requires an anomalous, supersingular, special-j, non-prime-order, or nonmonotone-q instance.
Any mandatory positive, curve, field-distinctness, global-seed, order, rho, resource, command, or verifier-linkage control fails.
Independent reconstruction or exact source-hash verification fails.
interpretation_limits: A finite-null pass would establish a toy additive-geometry signal on at least six scheduled curves, not stable family-wide behavior, split compression, or an ECDLP algorithm.
The 12-16 bit sweep cannot establish an exponent.
Rank, sparse linear algebra, factor-base logarithms, and individual target descent remain mandatory later gates.
The p mod 4 = 3 field restriction remains explicit.
hypothesis.mechanism: A coordinate-defined sign-complete set may expand more efficiently from four-term advice to eight-term coverage than independently seeded point-set null samples at matched cardinality, yielding an exact uniform-order fixed-curve coverage signal even when its four-term support is not compressed.

predictions.metric: exact eight-term support percentile against each finite-null sample
coverage efficiency |8A|/|4A|^2 percentile against each finite-null sample
exact uniform-order functional frontier percentile against each finite-null sample
each offline group-operation and charged field-cost ratio to median random-x
predictions.minimum_effect: at most 4.0 in every charged category

hypothesis.statement: At least one tested coordinate family passes the exploratory sign-complete eight-term coverage and exact uniform-order frontier gate against both finite-null samples on clean distinct-field curves.

instances: three deterministic clean prime-order curves per bit size over nine distinct field primes
